catalog_quote: [ThankGod & Ngulube 2022, p.57] Kari in his work on Central Delta Languages states that these languages have a two-tier tone system – a low tone ( ˋ) and a high tone ( ´), with a down-step . The down step occurs between two high tone vowels. Generally, tones in this language are marked on syllabic nasals and vowels. We shall employ in this work, this tonal rule to mark its tone. ... [p.59] In Abua, we observe that in SVC, verbs share a high tone, which evinces negativity. Abua HT is often indicated on the subjective form which occurs before the first verb in the serial construction. ... [Kari 2019, sec. 5.1] Tone is another interesting phonological characteristic of Rivers State languages. sources.citation: Kari, Ethelbert Emmanuel (2017). Central Delta languages: An overview. Stellenbosch Papers in Linguistics 47: 1-26. DOI 10.5774/47-0-213.
sources.quote: "Alex (1989:24) remarks that 'all Central Delta lects operate a basic two-tone system'. These tones are low tone, which is marked with a grave accent, and high tone, which is marked with an acute accent. There is also a downstep phenomenon in these languages. The downstep is marked with a small arrow pointing downwards between two high-toned syllables. Apart from the syllabic nasal, tone in these languages is anchored on vowels. Table 7 shows these tones and downstep as found in Abuan..." Abuan (Kari and Joshua 2011:8): òlòm 'husband', òlóꜜḿ 'to bite', ólóm 'paddle'. The word 'stress' occurs n
